description: Root defect exposed by fixtures2/behavior/repr_seam_enum_count_after_reduce2.fz at 0aa00f6f7: a generic/pooling BoundaryId is incorrectly treated as the ABI authority for concrete closure targets. The north-star contract requires callable-flow target identity to cross the artifact boundary, and callable-boundary lanes to use the selected target body's grounded representations. Current package_backend_callable_entries recovers captures only from concrete BoundaryFacts; direct-only concrete CallableFacts have resolutions but no BoundaryId, so an empty pooling fallback silently produces capture_count=0 for a three-input bridge body (one capture + two args). It also copies the pooling boundary's published return lanes [RawAtom, ValueRef] instead of the target body's [RawAtom, RawInt], so native rejects an invalid self-contradiction. Repair one data model: materialize a target-specific resolved callable-entry contract from concrete CallableFacts plus selected ExecutableKey, carry its identity on constructed closure values through generic publication, and derive capture/argument/grounded return lanes from that entry. Root packaging assigns dense entry ids; interpreter dispatches that id directly rather than reselecting by FunctionId/capture count/type overlap; native emits one thunk per entry and its boundary/body lanes agree by construction. Delete the empty-pooling ABI fallback, FunctionId-based interpreter reselection, and boundary-level return-lane derivation. Keep return adaptation only in existing CallReturnFlow/ReturnDelivery continuations. Regression proof: count-alone=2; reduce-then-count=10/2 on interp/run/build every run, target inputs equal capture+args, and every callable thunk's return lanes equal its target body.

comments.text: Validated the first deletion-only slice: native callable boundaries now derive return shape/reprs directly from the selected BackendExecutable return position; obsolete boundary-level return fields and unused pre-backend callable-entry structs are removed. LowerNativeProgram accepts the fixture and the compiled path now runs (no [RawAtom, ValueRef] vs [RawAtom, RawInt] boundary/body contradiction), but still prints 10/10. A carrier-lane spike proved the remaining defect is not return adaptation: a closure with a carrier capture still resolves by FunctionId to executable 65, whose body accepts only two runtime lanes. The required next slice is the ticket model: resolved callable-entry identity must be carried on constructed closure values and dispatched directly, replacing FunctionId/capture-count re-selection. No speculative carrier conversion remains in the branch.

While implementing the required no-reconstruction entry flow, direct lambda construction reached CallableId(1) with multiple concrete resolved entries. This is not a package-time ambiguity: the callable interner has already pooled distinct capture groundings, exactly fz-k22.18. Added fz-k22.18 -> fz-k22.20 dependency and am resolving the upstream identity fact first; no downstream target selection will be invented.

No-reselection spike moved to dedicated fz-k22 worktree. Concrete CallableFacts now package target-owned ABI entries and stamp construction sites, but with FunctionId/type-overlap fallback removed the fixture deterministically returns 2/2 rather than 10/2. This proves fz-k22.14 is an upstream blocker: CallTargetSummary has already collapsed the needed direct target before entry construction. Added fz-k22.14 -> fz-k22.20 dependency; will resolve that representation first rather than reintroduce selection.

Target fixture now prints 10/2 in interp/run/build with entry identity carried only for first-class published constructions. Native stores that resolved boundary on NativeBoundValue; direct-only callables retain direct artifact edges and no boundary inventory. Full lib suite is at 1313/1329 passing; remaining failures are legacy entry-inventory expectations and a few native publication paths being migrated to the entry-owned model.

Implemented the entry-owned closure ABI model without fallback reconstruction. Root packaging now records exact callable-entry identity by `(TransportPosition, CallableId)`, including nested tuple fields, returns, resume payloads, and entry captures. Backend and native consume that fact directly; native no longer selects by FunctionId, capture count, type overlap, or pooled BoundaryId. Target fixture `repr_seam_enum_count_after_reduce2` prints `10\n2` in interp/run/build. Verified `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check`, `cargo test --lib` (1329 passed, 0 failed, 6 ignored), and `git diff --check`. The remaining multi-entry Enum dispatch behavior is tracked on fz-1ah.11.

RETROSPECTIVE BATCH AUDIT FAIL at aadab3a24. The commit adds tagged-entry dispatch but does not complete its stated no-reselection deletion: src/ir_interp/backend.rs resolve_backend_callable_executable still selects untagged callables by FunctionId, capture count, ABI reprs, and runtime type overlap. The arc diff itself modified this function to add the entry fast path while retaining that fallback; its remaining production caller is fz_spawn/fz_spawn_opt in src/ir_interp/extern_call.rs. actor_ring succeeds only on the tagged route, so it is not proof the untagged fallback is impossible. Repair by making spawn consume the upstream entry identity or fail closed; remove the selector and add a regression that proves no first-class spawn callable can re-enter selection. Audit otherwise confirms exact entry propagation and target-owned ABI. Focused ownership tests passed; isolated fmt, clippy -D warnings, and cargo test --lib passed (1329 passed, 0 failed, 6 ignored). repr_seam_enum_count_after_reduce2, actor_ring, opaque_fn_value_join, and fz_f98_range_map_converges pass interp/run/build. enum_predicate_search and enum_take_drop_split remain explicit failures within already-tracked fz-1ah.11; no fallback selects a native target there.

ROOT-CAUSE TRACE (no implementation yet): Runtime demand already computes the required paired fact: CallableFlowFact.first_class_edges preserves each ground callable surface with its concrete ExecutableKey (runtime_demand.rs derive_callable_flow_facts_for_executable_product / callable_flow_resolution_edges_product). Transport then destroys that correlation. callable_for_producer passes per-surface resolution_symbols to publish_boundaries_for_callable, but TransportFactsBuilder records BoundaryFacts.publications and BoundaryFacts.resolutions through separate additive unions (transport.rs data model; jobs/transport.rs record_boundary + record_boundary_resolutions). resolve_publication_source_boundaries later unions source-derived resolutions again. Root packaging therefore has only a callable/boundary-wide target set: package_backend_callable_entries assigns a target by scanning CallableFacts.resolutions and finds a publication boundary with contains(target); materialize_callable_entry_positions can stamp a position only when that reconstructed set has exactly one entry. Any multi-entry publication stays unstamped. The backend interpreter then reaches resolve_backend_callable_executable through fz_spawn and repeats the lost selection from FunctionId/capture count/ABI/runtime type overlap.

Model repair: preserve a first-class publication-to-resolution edge upstream, not another fallback selector. Introduce a transport fact row keyed by the exact publication/construction TransportPosition plus CallableId and concrete ExecutableSymbol (or a typed equivalent). Derive it directly from CallableFlowFact.first_class_edges in publish_boundaries_for_callable and carry it through source/join/tuple/return/resume forwarding as data. Root packaging only densifies those already-paired resolution symbols into BackendCallableEntry identities; it must delete materialize_callable_entry_positions matching/filtering. Construction positions require one exact entry; forwarded values retain their existing runtime tag. A genuinely multi-entry first-class value must carry an upstream dispatch-entry plan (fz-1ah.11) or fail artifact formation before runtime—never select from a pooled boundary. This separates target-owned concrete ABI from boundary-owned invocation surface and makes fz_spawn consume the carried entry identity directly.

CLEAN-WORKTREE AUDIT PASS for f557a9c7d. Verified that the FunctionId/capture/type fallback symbols are absent; fz_spawn/fz_spawn_opt now consume only callable_entry_target, which fails closed without a carried identity. The new compiler2_interp_spawn_paths_carry_resolved_callable_entries regression covers named-function, captured-lambda, and nested actor-lambda spawn paths. Audit gates passed: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --lib (1330 passed, 0 failed, 6 ignored), and interp/run/build for actor_ring, spawn_with_captures, concurrency_ping_pong, and repr_seam_enum_count_after_reduce2. The multi-entry publication/dispatch fact remains correctly scoped to fz-1ah.11; this change does not reintroduce any selector.
